name: Domínguez and Escalante in the Great Basin
traveler: Francisco Atanasio Domínguez and Silvestre Vélez de Escalante
summary: Two Franciscan friars and eight companions set out from Santa Fe to find a road to the new missions of California. Guided by Ute people, they cross the Colorado Plateau and reach Utah Lake before snow turns them back; their map is the first of the Great Basin.

stops.note: Ten men set out, the same summer the thirteen colonies declare independence.
Guided by the Ute (Timpanogos), they reach a fertile valley and promise a mission.
Snow; they cast lots and decide to turn back.
A ford of the Colorado River they cut steps down to.
Home after five months and 2,800 km.

informs.note: The first map of the Colorado Plateau
Utah Lake and word of the lands beyond
